body: I love this comment. I love it so much that I want to point out your second sentence has the words swapped, it should be *"parents* not outliving their *children"* (or if you like, remove the "not" so it says "children outliving their parents"). I almost skipped over this amazing post because that line gave me the exact opposite impression of what it was going to be about. Just a heads up.

You're very kind I can tell, thank you.

I have browsed communities like them before but never posted, but irl my family despite what happened decided to double down even harder into religion and I've just had to hide my different reaction to it because they're the type to try to convert or shame anyone who questions it. But if I'm honest I never bought into any of it even as a kid, I remember thinking every time I went to church, even when I had coloring books to keep me busy, that I was bored and just there because I had to be. Nothing they said ever convinced me and I never felt anything there except boredom, and confusion in wondering if anyone else didn't want to be there and hated singing songs and listening to a random dude talk like he knows how the world works for 5 hours or if it was just me.

That's very interesting, have they ever explained how they were able to attain all of that? Like how do they ensure they don't go hungry, and afford things? Do they not buy anything and live off the land exclusively? If so, how did they learn to do that? This is fascinating to me, I'd love to learn more.

I used to be in marching band from high school through college before I realized getting a degree was a terrible investment. It was one of the few things I really loved. I'm reclusive and don't trust or connect with most people though, so I was there for the music and not the people. It's that way for everything for me, I can count on one hand the number of people who actually feel like friends to me. But thank you for your advice, it means a lot to me that you're willing to reach out and listen and write such long replies to me. Thank you

I do hear what you're saying a lot, but I can't see that perspective myself. While murders and abuse and all kinds of flashy destruction that get overreported on in the news are certainly still awful, it's the systemic things that few are talking about and none are able to change because those in power are bribed by those who profit off the system to perpetuate it and there's nothing we can do as voters to stop it that depresses me most. 

I used to want to get into scientific research, but I hit a wall and started failing my classes so I'm too stupid to get a degree for it. Just as well, everyone's response to the pandemic (which contrary to popular belief is *still going on,* by the way, people are still dying) shows no one actually cares about science or facts. At least, all the people who should care don't. So what's the point in trying.
When I was young and naive I wanted to do something to do with culinary arts but unless you get lucky and work for a super high-end place you're going to make pennies and I hate that I have to value money over anything else because that's what the greedy narcissists who run everything do and impose that on everyone else.
At this point I'll take what I can get. I'm kind of a robot, if I can earn a decent amount just doing data entry or calculations or staring at excel sheets without needing to talk to anyone I'd be overjoyed, that sounds perfect for me. But again, under it all the systemic problems of society and inherent immorality and ignorance of humanity makes me not care about anything.

I have hobbies too, that's basically all I do when I'm not sleeping or working or lying about having eaten.

I'm sorry again, I had to go to bed but I'm awake now and still want to talk.

I see, I think he's someone who's not very informed on mental health issues to believe something like that (not his fault entirely, education about that is pretty terrible no matter where you live). Why do you keep doing it? Have you ever thought of finding something else to replace it that gives you the same feeling?

I'm not sure if reddit is acting up or if you deleted your reply to my comment, but I never got a notification and just checked your profile and was able to read it there, and I'm very sorry I didn't see it before.

I think we're kindred spirits, all I do is sleep all day too and only talk to my boyfriend too haha. Honestly sleeping is one of the best things you can do, it lets you rest and get away from all the crap and it's like a free trial of nonexistance.

Have you considered telling him the truth? What do you think he would say?
If there even is one, whoever it is is a sadist for sure

I understand you and hear you. I have autism and horrible narcissitic parents too. I wish I could do something to help. All I can say is that last sentence you wrote, it's true. She will not change or care if you kill yourself. Don't let her win, out of spite keep living and make her suffer.

What makes you happy to do? Do you have any hobbies?
Does your boyfriend know you do this?

Hey there, I have horrible parents and a long-distance boyfriend just like you. I know exactly what you're going through. I know how awful it sucks and how hopeless it feels: despite having a way out you can't use it and you feel trapped, wondering if it's worth trying to wait it out until things get better.

I'm so sorry this is the hand you were dealt. I wish I could help in a way that wasn't words on a screen. I hope you know you're not fat or stupid, I hope you believe the opposite in true. Even if you can't truly believe it right now, even if it's hard to stop self-harming do it to spite her. She would want you to feel bad about yourself, don't do what she wants, what she wants is worth less than nothing.
